blocks.p: At last a grave-looking person came to the gate, named Good-will, who asked who was there, where he had come from, and what he wanted.

“Here is a poor burdened sinner,” said Christian. “I come from the City of Destruction, but I am going to Mount Zion, so that I may be delivered from the wrath to come. And since I’m told that the way there goes through this gate, sir, I’d like to know whether you are willing to let me in.”
“I am willing with all my heart,” he said; and with that he opened the gate.
Just as Christian was stepping in, Good-will gave him a sharp pull.
“What was that for?” said Christian.

“A little distance from this gate,” the other told him, “stands a strong castle, and Beelzebub is its captain. From there he and those with him shoot arrows at anyone who comes up to this gate, hoping they may die before they can get in.”
“I rejoice and tremble,” said Christian.
When he was inside, the man at the gate asked him who had directed him there.
“Evangelist told me to come here and knock, as I did; and he said that you, sir, would tell me what I must do.”
“An open door is set before you, and no one can shut it.”
“Now I begin to reap the benefits of the risks I’ve taken.”
“But how is it that you came alone?”
“Because none of my neighbors saw their danger as I saw mine.”
“Did any of them know you were coming?”

“Yes. My wife and children saw me at the start and called after me to turn back. Some of my neighbors also stood crying and calling for me to come back. But I put my fingers in my ears, and so came on my way.”
“But didn’t any of them follow you, to persuade you to go back?”
“Yes, both Obstinate and Pliable. But when they saw they couldn’t win me over, Obstinate went back railing at me, while Pliable came with me a little way.”
“But why didn’t he come through?”

“We did come together, until we reached the Swamp of Despair, and there we both suddenly fell in. Then my neighbor Pliable was discouraged and wouldn’t risk going further. So he got out on the side nearest his own house, and told me I could have the wonderful country to myself. He went his way and I came mine: he after Obstinate, and I to this gate.”
“Alas, poor man!” said Good-will. “Does he think so little of heavenly glory that he doesn’t consider it worth the risk of a few difficulties to obtain it?”

“To be honest,” said Christian, “I’ve told you the truth about Pliable; but if I tell you the whole truth about myself, it will be plain there is nothing to choose between us. It’s true that he went back to his own house; but I also turned aside onto the road of death, persuaded by the worldly arguments of a certain Mr. Worldly Wiseman.”
“Oh, did he find you? What! He would have had you look for relief at the hands of Mr. Legality. They are both of them nothing but frauds. But did you take his advice?”
“Yes, as far as I dared. I went to find Mr. Legality, until I thought the mountain that stands by his house was going to fall on my head; and there I was forced to stop.”
“That mountain has been the death of many, and will be the death of many more. It’s a good thing you escaped being dashed to pieces by it.”

“Why, truly, I don’t know what would have become of me there if Evangelist hadn’t happened to meet me again while I stood brooding in my misery. It was God’s mercy that he came to me again, or I would never have come here. But now I have come, such as I am, more fit, indeed, to be crushed by that mountain than to stand here talking with my lord. But oh, what a favor this is to me, that I am still allowed in here!”

“We raise no objections against anyone, no matter what they have done before they came here. They are never turned away. [John 6:37] And so, good Christian, come a little way with me, and I will teach you about the road you must take. Look ahead of you. Do you see this narrow road? That is the road you must take. It was laid down by the patriarchs, the prophets, Christ, and his apostles, and it is as straight as a ruler can make it. This is the way you must go.”
“But,” said Christian, “are there no turnings or windings where a stranger might lose his way?”
“Yes, there are many roads that run into this one, and they are crooked and wide. But this is how you can tell the right from the wrong: the right one alone is straight and narrow.” [Matt. 7:14]

Then I saw in my dream that Christian asked him further whether he could help him take off the burden on his back; for he had not yet got rid of it, and could not get it off by any means without help.
“As for your burden,” Good-will told him, “be content to carry it until you come to the place of deliverance; for there it will fall from your back by itself.”

Then Christian tightened his belt and set himself to his journey. The other told him that when he had gone some distance from the gate, he would come to the house of the Interpreter, and that he should knock at the door, and the Interpreter would show him excellent things. Then Christian said goodbye to his friend, and Good-will once again wished him Godspeed.
